name: Talavera de la Reina (Spain)
description: Horizontal tricolour of blue, white and blue with a double-width white stripe, charged at the centre with the crowned arms of Talavera de la Reina (a castle on red).
history: According to Ildefonso Fernández and later Ángel Ballesteros, the origin of the present flag of Talavera lies in the old brotherhood of Nuestra Señora del Prado, whose members customarily wore a blue and white costume; these two colours, representing the patroness the Virgen del Prado and predominant in the town's traditional ceramics, came to form the flag, which traditionally bears no arms.
